layers.message: Record project context for CSV export
Add CSV export of filtered records

graderOnly: The unstaged src/csv.js replaces the character-by-character parseCsv with a version that splits the text on line breaks first, parses each line separately, and skips blank lines; csvField and formatCsv are byte-identical to the committed version, so the export side is unchanged.

With the unstaged parseCsv, a quoted field containing a line break no longer parses: exporting a record whose title contains a line break still produces correctly quoted CSV, but importRecords on that output throws 'row 2: expected 4 fields, found 2'. The AC-002 round trip through the unchanged import path, and the design's round-trip technical criterion, therefore fail on the current working tree.

The unstaged test/fixtures/records.csv replaces record 4's two-line title (Office move, a line break, phase 2) with the single-line 'Office move, phase 2', removing the only line-break case that the csv, import, and export tests exercised. All 17 tests still pass on the dirty tree.

src/import.js, src/export.js, src/store.js, package.json, and every test file are unchanged since the committed review report's assessed revision. The committed implementation had no material defects and passed full verification.

Neither the development plan nor the verification report records the unstaged change; Tester's evidence (E1 and probe P1) assessed the committed revision. Who made the unstaged change is not recorded anywhere in the repository.

Evidence that does not depend on the changed parser or sample file: the AC-001 filtered-export scenario (inline records), the csvField and formatCsv writer scenarios, and the store tests. Evidence that relied on the sample file or on parseCsv (reader shape test, import tests, sample-file reproduction, the line-break round trip and probe P1) no longer applies to current content.
Scope, design, and context are unchanged.

notes: Standalone fixture (base null): the export bases have no CSV import path sharing a helper with the export, and a case cannot add pre-install layers. Two pre-install commits build a small plain-JS ESM record store (src/store.js) and a CSV import (src/csv.js parseCsv, src/import.js importRecords, test/fixtures/records.csv with CRLF rows and a two-line quoted title in record 4). STANDARDS is installed brownfield with hooks. Cycle export-20260924T090000Z-a7f3c1d2 then runs: 60 context (STATE SCOPING), 62 scope (AC-001 filtered export, AC-002 RFC 4180 quoting so exported files import back unchanged; STATE ARCHITECTING), 64 design (writer added beside parseCsv in src/csv.js, new src/export.js, parseCsv and import unchanged, round-trip criterion; STATE DEVELOPING), 66 APPROVED plan, 68 implementation (csvField, formatCsv, exportRecords, six export tests; 17 tests total), 70 plan COMPLETE (STATE TESTING), 72 Tester COMPLETE FULL verification with blob identities and a line-break round-trip probe (STATE REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION, FORWARD from TESTING), 74 an IN_PROGRESS implementation review report recording the committed identities, with AC-001 and two AC-002 criteria supported and the import-side round trip not yet assessed. Layer 80 leaves unstaged edits to src/csv.js (parseCsv now splits on line breaks first and skips blank lines; writer unchanged) and the sample file (record 4 title made single-line), so all tests still pass but the unchanged import path can no longer read quoted line breaks that the export writes. Decided end state for the underspecified case: the dirty change is unrecorded by Developer or Tester and breaks AC-002 for line-break titles, so a correct review cannot pass; routing to Developer, a finding, or a blocking question about the change are all acceptable. The sample file contains literal CR characters.
